title: Smart Data Models - TM Forum Open APIs - Resource
description: Resource is an abstract entity that describes the common set of attributes shared by all concrete resources (e.g. TPE, EQUIPMENT) in the inventory. (TM Forum TMF639 Resource Inventory Management 5.0.0, OpenAPI component Resource, with the attributes of its sub-classes LogicalResource, PhysicalResource, SoftwareResource, ResourceFunction flattened in; attribute names kept verbatim except the NGSI-LD reserved terms / JSON-LD keywords renamed with a tmf prefix (id, @type, @baseType, @schemaLocation, ...); deprecated attributes left out.)

id.description: Property. Unique identifier of the entity: urn:ngsi-ld:Resource:<tmfId>.

type.description: Property. NGSI-LD Entity type. It must be equal to 'Resource'

dateModified.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/DateTime'. Timestamp of the last modification.

source.description: Property. A sequence of characters giving the original source of the entity data.

dataProvider.description: Property. A sequence of characters identifying the provider of the harmonised data entity.

Renamed from TMF '@type' (JSON-LD keyword). TMF class name of the instance: 'Resource' or a sub-class / extension name. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-class Extensible name

startOperatingDate.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/startOperatingDate'. The point in time from which the resource is operating

endOperatingDate.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/endOperatingDate'. The point in time till the resource is operating

operationalState.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/operationalState'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceOperationalState' of a Resource; the operational state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) tracks whether or not the resource is installed and working; it is single valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'disabled': The resource is totally inoperable and unable to provide service to the user(s); 'enabled': The resource is partially or fully operable and available for use.

usageState.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/usageState'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceUsageState' of a Resource; the usage state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) tracks whether the resource is currently in use and if it can accept additional users or not; it is single-valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'idle': The resource is not currently in use; 'active': The resource is in use, and has sufficient spare operating capacity to provide for additional users simultaneously; 'busy': The resource is in use, but it has no spare operating capacity to provide for additional users at this instant.

administrativeState.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/administrativeState'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceAdministrativeState' of a Resource; the administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents permission to use ('unlocked') or prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed through the management services; it is single valued and read-write by management functions; defined values: 'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from performing services for its users; 'shutdown': Use of the resource is administratively permitted to existing instances of use only. While the system remains in the shutting down state the manager may at any time cause the managed object to revert to the unlocked state; 'unlocked': The resource is administratively permitted to perform services for its users; this is independent of its inherent operability.

lifecycleState.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/lifecycleState'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceLifecycleState' of a Resource; the lifecycle state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents the planned and tracked state of a physical or logical resource; it is single valued and read-write by management functions; defined values: 'planned', 'installed', 'pendingRemoval'

alarmStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/alarmStatus'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-valued and read-only by management functions, each value represents an existing severity; defined values: 'underRepair': The resource is currently being repaired; 'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and have not been cleared; 'major': One or more major alarms indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and have not yet been cleared; 'minor': One or more minor alarms indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and have not yet been cleared; 'alarmOutstanding': One or more alarms have been detected in the resource. The condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause of the condition and the services that are affected.

proceduralStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/proceduralStatus'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceProceduralStatus' of a Resource; the procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents a sequence of phases through which the resource needs to progress; it is single valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'initializationRequired': The resource requires initialization to be invoked by the manager before it can perform its normal functions, and this procedure has not been initiated. The manager may be able to invoke such initialization through an action. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'notInitialized': The resource requires initialization before it can perform its normal functions, and this procedure has not been initiated. The resource initializes itself autonomously, but the operational state may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource requires initialization before it can perform its normal functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class definition; 'reporting': The resource has completed some processing operation and is notifying the results of the operation, e.g., a test process is sending its results. The operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize itself autonomously, the operational state is 'disabled'. Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class definition

availabilityStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/availabilityStatus'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceAvailabilityStatus' of a Resource; the availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents the availability of the resource for either carrying service or for being in other states, such as in testing; it is single valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'inTest': The resource is undergoing a test procedure. If the administrative state is 'locked' or 'shuttingDown', then normal users are precluded from using the resource, and the controlStatus attribute has the value 'reservedForTest'. Tests that do not exclude additional users can be present in any operational or administrative state but the 'reservedForTest' condition should not be present; 'failed': The resource has an internal fault that prevents it from operating. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'powerOff': The resource requires power to be applied and is not powered on. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'online': The resource is available for use. The operational state is 'enabled'; 'offline': The resource requires a routine operation to be performed to place it on line and make it available for use. The operation may be manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive by an internal control process in accordance with a predetermined time schedule. Under normal conditions the control process can be expected to reactivate the resource at some scheduled time, and it is therefore considered to be optional. The operational state is 'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot operate because some other resource on which it depends (i.e., a resource not represented by the same managed object) is unavailable. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'degraded': The service available from the resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or operating capacity. Failure of a test or an unacceptable performance measurement has established that some or all services are not functional or are degraded due to the presence of a defect. However, the resource remains available for service, either because some services are satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to no service at all. Object specific attributes may be defined to represent further information indicating, for example, which services are not functional and the nature of the degradation. The operational state is 'enabled'; 'notInstalled': The resource represented by the managed object is not present, or is incomplete. The operational state is 'disabled'; 'logFull': This indicates a log full condition, which means that the maximum capacity of the log has been reached

controlStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/controlStatus'. Value enumeration for the 'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at unpredictable times, which may cause it to exhibit unusual characteristics to users; 'partOfServicesLocked': This value indicates whether a manager has administratively restricted a particular part of a service from the user(s) of a resource. The administrative state is 'unlocked'. Examples are incoming service barred, outgoing service barred, write locked by media key, read locked; 'reservedForTest': The resource has been made administratively unavailable to normal users because it is undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is 'locked'; 'suspended': Service has been administratively suspended to the users of the resource. The resource may retain knowledge of current users and/or requests for usage, depending upon the managed object class definition, but does not resume performing services until the suspended condition is revoked. The administrative state is 'unlocked'

Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/supportingResource'. resourceRelationship.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/resourceRelationship'. resourceCharacteristic.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/resourceCharacteristic'. A list of Characteristics of this resource

attachment.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/attachment'. A list of references to attachments associated with this resource

resourceSpecification.description: Relationship. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/resourceSpecification'. Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within an enterprise's infrastructure or inventory. They are typically consumed or used by services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content and information, and technology components. A ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of Resource. In essence, a ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that is based on a particular ResourceSpecification. In TMF this is a ResourceSpecificationRef object; here the NGSI-LD id of the referenced ResourceSpecification entity (urn:ngsi-ld:ResourceSpecification:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

resourceVersion.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/resourceVersion'. A field that identifies the specific version of an instance of a resource. NOTE: At some point in the future (v6) this will be aligned with the new Version pattern, and then this property would need to be renamed to **version**.

Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/intent'. Intent reference, for when Intent is used by other entities. In TMF this is a IntentRef object; here the NGSI-LD id of the referenced Intent entity (urn:ngsi-ld:Intent:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

externalIdentifier.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/Resource/properties/externalIdentifier'. An identification of this resource that is owned by or originates in a software system different from the current system. The structure identifies the system itself, the nature of the resource within the system and the unique ID of the resource within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single resource, e.g. if the resource passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system.

tmfValue.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/LogicalResource/properties/value'. E.g '0746712345' for MSISDN's

manufactureDate.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/PhysicalResource/properties/manufactureDate'. Only for TMF sub-class PhysicalResource (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). This is a string attribute that defines the date of manufacture of this item in the ISO 8601 date time standard format. This is an optional attribute.

standbyStatus.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/PhysicalResource/properties/standbyStatus'. Only for TMF sub-class PhysicalResource (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Value enumeration for the 'resourceStandbyStatus' of a Resource; the standby status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents the working mode for standby objects, i.e. whether it is providing service or standby as a back-up resource; it is single valued and read-only by management functions; defined values: 'hotStandby': The resource is not providing service, but is operating in synchronism with another resource that is to be backed-up (e.g., a computer shadowing another computer). A resource with a hot standby status will be immediately able to take over the role of the resource to be backed up, without the need for initialization activity, and will contain the same information as the resource to be backed up; 'coldStandby': The resource is to back up another resource, but is not synchronized with that resource. A resource with a cold standby status will not be immediately able to take over the role of a resource to be backed up, and will require some initialization activity; 'providingService': The back up resource is providing service and is backing up another resource.

powerConsumingState.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/PhysicalResource/properties/powerConsumingState'. Only for TMF sub-class PhysicalResource (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Value enumeration for the 'resourcePowerConsumingState' of a Resource; the power consuming state attribute (defined by ITU-T M.3701) indicates the power consuming policy of the resource represented by the managed object, it is single valued and read-write by management functions.; defined values: 'fullPower': The resource runs in full power and will not consider power saving. If a large device contains parts that also support this attribute, when the container object set to full power state, all its parts shall turn into full power state; 'powerSaving': The resource is (or may be) partially running to save power; depending on how much the payload is lower than the maximum capacity of the resource, the degree of saving will be automatically decided by the resource. If power saving is not supported by the resource, attempting to change to this state will have the same effect as full power state. If a large device contains parts that also support this attribute, when the container object is set to power saving state, its parts may still remain in full power state. But if one of the parts turns into power saving state, the container object shall turn into power saving state; 'sleeping': The resource is not running but keeps a snapshot of its memory before sleeping, and can resume running mode quickly. In this mode, the power is only consumed to meet the need of maintaining the memory. If it is not supported by the resource, attempting to change to this state will result in a failure; 'shutdown': The resource has been powered off and does not consume any more power; if it is not supported by the resource, attempting to change to this state will result in a failure.

powerConsumingLevel.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/PhysicalResource/properties/powerConsumingLevel'. Only for TMF sub-class PhysicalResource (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). The power consuming level attribute (defined by ITU-T M.3701) indicates the current percentage of power consuming of the resource represented by the managed object, where 100 percent represents the maximum power consumption of the device. It is single valued and read-only by management functions.

serialNumber.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/PhysicalResource/properties/serialNumber'. This is a string that represents a manufacturer-allocated number used to identify different instances of the same hardware item. The ModelNumber and PartNumber attributes are used to identify different types of hardware items.

batchNumber.description: Property. lastUpdate.description: Property. Only for TMF sub-class SoftwareResource (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Defines the target platform that the SoftwareResource will be deployed on.

connectionPoint.description: Property. Only for TMF sub-class ResourceFunction (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Internal connectivity of contained resource functions.

priority.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceFunction/properties/priority'. Only for TMF sub-class ResourceFunction (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Priority of the Resource Function. Decides what happens in a contention scenario.

role.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceFunction/properties/role'. Only for TMF sub-class ResourceFunction (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). Role of the Resource Function. Used when Resource Function is a component of a composite Resource Function and the exact role of the service within the composite is not clear from descriptor/location.

functionType.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF639_ResourceInventory/blob/v5.0.0/TMF639-Resource_Inventory_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceFunction/properties/functionType'. Only for TMF sub-class ResourceFunction (flattened into Resource; set tmfType accordingly). A type of the Resource Function as specified by the provider of the API.

autoModification.description: Property. allOf.description: An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different from the current system, for example a ProductOrder handed off from a commerce platform into an order handling system. The structure identifies the system itself, the nature of the entity within the system (e.g. class name) and the unique ID of the entity within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this case the consumer is expected to sequence the IDs in the array in reverse order of provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
